Screening

One engine, one return shape, whichever rule is applied.

Screen response times with any rule
rt_keep()
Keep vector from a screening rule
screen_fits()

Combining rules

No single conventional rule reaches both the slow tail and the leading edge; these put two together.

rule_all() rule_any() rule_then()
Combine screening rules
rule_hierarchical()
Hierarchical screening

Reporting

The Methods paragraph a screen owes a reader, written from the screen rather than from memory.

report_screening()
Report a screening procedure in prose
format(<rtprep_report>) print(<rtprep_report>) as.character(<rtprep_report>) toBibtex(<rtprep_report>)
Methods for a screening report

Aggregation and estimation

From surviving trials to EZ-diffusion inputs and parameters.

rt_summary()
Aggregate response times into EZ-diffusion summary statistics
adjust_accuracy()
Correct accuracy counts for contamination
ez_ddm()
Invert summary statistics into diffusion parameters

Comparison and diagnostics

What a different choice would have removed, and whether the removed trials were what you thought.

screen_compare() print(<rtprep_comparison>) summary(<rtprep_comparison>) print(<rtprep_comparison_summary>) plot(<rtprep_comparison>)
Compare what several screening rules would remove
check_guessing()
Test whether the fast trials a rule removed were really guesses

Ground truth

Generate data whose contaminants are labelled, and remove exactly those, so a screen can be scored and read against perfect exclusion.

r_contaminated()
Generate response time data with contaminants of known type
